items.text: It is narrated on the authority of Amirul Mu'minin, Abu Hafs 'Umar bin al-Khattab (ra) who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "Actions are (judged) by motives (niyyah), so each man will have what he intended. Thus, he whose migration (hijrah) was to Allah and His Messenger, his migration is to Allah and His Messenger; but he whose migration was for some worldly thing he might gain, or for a wife he might marry, his migration is to that for which he migrated." [Bukhari & Muslim]

items.text: Also on the authority of ʿUmar (ra) who said: While we were one day sitting with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ there appeared before us a man dressed in extremely white clothes and with very black hair. No traces of journeying were visible on him, and none of us knew him. He sat down close by the Prophet ﷺ rested his knees against the knees of the Prophet ﷺ and placed his palms over his thighs, and said: "O Muhammad! Inform me about Islam." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ replied: "Islam is that you should testify that there is no deity worthy of worship except Allah and that Muhammad is His Messenger ﷺ, that you should perform salah (ritual prayer), pay the zakah, fast during Ramadan, and perform Hajj (pilgrimage) to the House (the Kaʿbah at Makkah), if you can find a way to it (or find the means for making the journey to it)." He said: "You have spoken the truth." We were astonished at his thus questioning him ﷺ and then telling him that he was right, but he went on to say, "Inform me about Iman (faith)." He (the Prophet) answered, "It is that you believe in Allah and His angels and His Books and His Messengers and in the Last Day, and in fate (qadar), both in its good and in its evil aspects." He said, "You have spoken the truth." Then he (the man) said, "Inform me about Ihsan." He (the Prophet) answered, "It is that you should serve Allah as though you could see Him, for though you cannot see Him yet He sees you." He said, "Inform me about the Hour." He (the Prophet) said, "About that the one questioned knows no more than the questioner." So he said, "Well, inform me about its signs." He said, "They are that the slave-girl will give birth to her mistress and that you will see the barefooted ones, the naked, the destitute, the herdsmen of the sheep (competing with each other) in raising lofty buildings." Thereupon the man went off. I waited a while, and then he (the Prophet) said, "O ʿUmar, do you know who that questioner was?" I replied, "Allah and His Messenger know better." He said, "That was Jibril. He came to teach you your religion." [Muslim]

items.text: On the authority of Abdullah ibn Masood (ra), who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he is the truthful, the believed, narrated to us, “Verily the creation of each one of you is brought together in his mother’s womb for forty days in the form of a nutfah (a drop), then he becomes an alaqah (clot of blood) for a like period, then a mudghah (morsel of flesh) for a like period, then there is sent to him the angel who blows his soul into him and who is commanded with four matters: to write down his rizq (sustenance), his life span, his actions, and whether he will be happy or unhappy (i.e., whether or not he will enter Paradise). By the One, other than Whom there is no deity, verily one of you performs the actions of the people of Paradise until there is but an arms length between him and it, and that which has been written overtakes him, and so he acts with the actions of the people of the Hellfire and thus enters it; and verily one of you performs the actions of the people of the Hellfire, until there is but an arms length between him and it, and that which has been written overtakes him and so he acts with the actions of the people of Paradise and thus he enters it.” [Bukhari & Muslim]

items.text: On the authority of an-Nu’man ibn Basheer (ra), who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say, “That which is lawful is clear and that which is unlawful is clear, and between the two of them are doubtful matters about which many people do not know. Thus he who avoids doubtful matters clears himself in regard to his religion and his honor, but he who falls into doubtful matters [eventually] falls into that which is unlawful, like the shepherd who pastures around a sanctuary, all but grazing therein. Truly every king has a sanctuary, and truly Allah’s sanctuary is His prohibitions. Truly in the body there is a morsel of flesh, which, if it be whole, all the body is whole, and which, if it is diseased, all of [the body] is diseased. Truly, it is the heart.” [Bukhari & Muslim]

items.text: On the authority of Abu Hurayrah (ra): The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, “Allah the Almighty is Good and accepts only that which is good. And verily Allah has commanded the believers to do that which He has commanded the Messengers. So the Almighty has said: “O (you) Messengers! Eat of the tayyibat [all kinds of halal (legal) foods], and perform righteous deeds.” [23: 51] and the Almighty has said: “O you who believe! Eat of the lawful things that We have provided you.” [2: 172]” Then he ﷺ mentioned [the case] of a man who, having journeyed far, is disheveled and dusty, and who spreads out his hands to the sky saying “O Lord! O Lord!,” while his food is haram (unlawful), his drink is haram, his clothing is haram, and he has been nourished with haram, so how can [his supplication] be answered? [Muslim]

items.text: On the authority of Abu Abbas Abdullah bin Abbas (may Allah be pleased with him) who said: One day I was behind the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) [riding on the same mount] and he said, “O young man, I shall teach you some words [of advice]: Be mindful of Allah and Allah will protect you. Be mindful of Allah and you will find Him in front of you. If you ask, then ask Allah [alone]; and if you seek help, then seek help from Allah [alone]. And know that if the nation were to gather together to benefit you with anything, they would not benefit you except with what Allah had already prescribed for you. And if they were to gather together to harm you with anything, they would not harm you except with what Allah had already prescribed against you. The pens have been lifted and the pages have dried.” It was related by at-Tirmidhi, who said it was a good and sound hadeeth. Another narration, other than that of Tirmidhi, reads: Be mindful of Allah, and you will find Him in front of you. Recognize and acknowledge Allah in times of ease and prosperity, and He will remember you in times of adversity. And know that what has passed you by [and you have failed to attain] was not going to befall you, and what has befallen you was not going to pass you by. And know that victory comes with patience, relief with affliction, and hardship with ease

And the salah (prayer) is a light, and charity is a proof, and patience is illumination, and the Qur’an is a proof either for you or against you. Every person starts his day as a vendor of his soul, either freeing it or causing its ruin.” [Muslim]

items.text: On the authority of Abu Dharr al-Ghifaree (may Allah be pleased with him) from the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) from his Lord, that He said: O My servants! I have forbidden dhulm (oppression) for Myself, and I have made it forbidden amongst you, so do not oppress one another. O My servants, all of you are astray except those whom I have guided, so seek guidance from Me and I shall guide you. O My servants, all of you are hungry except those whom I have fed, so seek food from Me and I shall feed you. O My servants, all of you are naked except those whom I have clothed, so seek clothing from Me and I shall clothe you. O My servants, you commit sins by day and by night, and I forgive all sins, so seek forgiveness from Me and I shall forgive you. O My servants, you will not attain harming Me so as to harm Me, and you will not attain benefiting Me so as to benefit Me. O My servants, if the first of you and the last of you, and the humans of you and the jinn of you, were all as pious as the most pious heart of any individual amongst you, then this would not increase My Kingdom an iota. O My servants, if the first of you and the last of you, and the humans of you and the jinn of you, were all as wicked as the most wicked heart of any individual amongst you, then this would not decrease My Kingdom an iota. O My servants, if the first of you and the last of you, and the humans of you and the jinn of you, were all to stand together in one place and ask of Me, and I were to give everyone what he requested, then that would not decrease what I Possess, except what is decreased of the ocean when a needle is dipped into it. O My servants, it is but your deeds that I account for you, and then recompense you for. So he who finds good, let him praise Allah, and he who finds other than that, let him blame no one but himself. [Muslim]

items.text: Also on the authority of Abu Dharr (may Allah be pleased with him): Some people from amongst the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said to the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him), "O Messenger of Allah, the affluent have made off with the rewards; they pray as we pray, they fast as we fast, and they give [much] in charity by virtue of their wealth." He (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said, "Has not Allah made things for you to give in charity? Truly every tasbeehah [saying: 'subhan-Allah'] is a charity, and every takbeerah [saying: 'Allahu akbar'] is a charity, and every tahmeedah [saying: 'al-hamdu lillah'] is a charity, and every tahleelah [saying: 'laa ilaha illAllah'] is a charity. And commanding the good is a charity, and forbidding an evil is a charity, and in the budʿi [sexual act] of each one of you there is a charity." They said, "O Messenger of Allah, when one of us fulfils his carnal desire will he have some reward for that?" He (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said, "Do you not see that if he were to act upon it [his desire] in an unlawful manner then he would be deserving of punishment? Likewise, if he were to act upon it in a lawful manner then he will be deserving of a reward." [Muslim]

To help a man with his mount, lifting him onto it or hoisting up his belongings onto it, is a charity. And the good word is a charity. items.text: On the authority of an-Nawas bin Sam’an (may Allah be pleased with him), that the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said: Righteousness is in good character, and wrongdoing is that which wavers in your soul, and which you dislike people finding out about. [Muslim] And on the authority of Wabisah bin Ma’bad (may Allah be pleased with him) who said: I came to the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) and he (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said, “You have come to ask about righteousness.” I said, “Yes.” He (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said, “Consult your heart. Righteousness is that about which the soul feels at ease and the heart feels tranquil. And wrongdoing is that which wavers in the soul and causes uneasiness in the breast, even though people have repeatedly given their legal opinion [in its favour].” A good hadeeth transmitted from the musnads of the two imams, Ahmed bin Hambal and Al- Darimi, with a good chain of authorities

items.text: On the authority of Abu Najeeh al-’Irbaad ibn Saariyah (may Allah be pleased with him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) gave us a sermon by which our hearts were filled with fear and tears came to our eyes. So we said, “O Messenger of Allah! It is as though this is a farewell sermon, so counsel us.” He (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said, “I counsel you to have taqwa (fear) of Allah, and to listen and obey [your leader], even if a slave were to become your ameer. Verily he among you who lives long will see great controversy, so you must keep to my Sunnah and to the Sunnah of the Khulafa ar-Rashideen (the rightly guided caliphs), those who guide to the right way. Cling to it stubbornly [literally: with your molar teeth]. Beware of newly invented matters [in the religion], for verily every bidah (innovation) is misguidance.” [Abu Dawud] It was related by at-Tirmidhi, who said that it was a good and sound hadeeth

items.text: On the authority of Muadh bin Jabal (may Allah be pleased with him) who said: I said, “O Messenger of Allah, tell me of an act which will take me into Paradise and will keep me away from the Hellfire.” He (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said, “You have asked me about a great matter, yet it is easy for him for whom Allah makes it easy: worship Allah, without associating any partners with Him; establish the prayer; pay the zakat; fast in Ramadhan; and make the pilgrimage to the House.” Then he (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said, “Shall I not guide you towards the means of goodness? Fasting is a shield; charity wipes away sin as water extinguishes fire; and the praying of a man in the depths of the night.” Then he (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) recited: “[Those] who forsake their beds, to invoke their Lord in fear and hope, and they spend (charity in Allah’s cause) out of what We have bestowed on them. No person knows what is kept hidden for them of joy as a reward for what they used to do.” [as-Sajdah, 16-17] Then he (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said, “Shall I not inform you of the head of the matter, its pillar and its peak?” I said, “Yes, O Messenger of Allah.” He (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said, “The head of the matter is Islam, its pillar is the prayer and its peak is jihad.” Then he (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said, “Shall I not tell you of the foundation of all of that?” I said, “Yes, O Messenger of Allah.” So he took hold of his tongue and said, “Restrain this.” I said, “O Prophet ﷺ of Allah, will we be taken to account for what we say with it?” He (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said, “May your mother be bereaved of you, O Muadh! Is there anything that throws people into the Hellfire upon their faces — or: on their noses — except the harvests of their tongues?” It was related by at-Tirmidhi, who said it was a good and sound hadeeth

Why should I keep studying?

items.text: Those things he takes most delight in are often the most injurious to him, and those things which benefit him are not to be obtained without toil and trouble.
items.ref: al-Ghazali, The Alchemy of Happiness, ch. 1, p. 29 (tr. Claud Field, 1910)
items.topic: effort, hard work, good things need effort
ask: Why is learning hard sometimes?

items.text: When a man further considers how his various wants of food, lodging, etc., are amply supplied from the storehouse of creation, he becomes aware that God's mercy is as great as His power and wisdom, as He has Himself said, "My mercy is greater than My wrath," and according to the Prophet's saying, "God is more tender to His servants than a mother to her suckling-child."
items.ref: al-Ghazali, The Alchemy of Happiness, ch. 2, p. 32 (tr. Claud Field, 1910)
items.topic: gratitude, God's mercy, blessings of food and home
ask: How does Allah take care of us?
Why should I be thankful?

items.text: In short, each of us is entrusted with a little kingdom, and charged not to be careless in the administration of it.
items.ref: al-Ghazali, The Alchemy of Happiness, ch. 2, p. 35 (tr. Claud Field, 1910)
items.topic: responsibility for yourself, self-discipline
ask: Am I responsible for my own actions?

items.text: Love is the seed of happiness, and love to God is fostered and developed by worship. Such worship and constant remembrance of God implies a certain degree of austerity and curbing of bodily appetites.
items.ref: al-Ghazali, The Alchemy of Happiness, ch. 2, p. 38 (tr. Claud Field, 1910)
items.topic: love of Allah, worship, remembrance of Allah, self-discipline
ask: How do I grow my love for Allah?

items.text: Even the Prophet of God said, "I am a man like you, and get angry like others"; and in the Koran it is written, "God loves those who swallow down their anger," not those who have no anger at all.
items.ref: al-Ghazali, The Alchemy of Happiness, ch. 2, p. 40 (tr. Claud Field, 1910)
items.topic: controlling anger, swallowing anger
ask: Is it a sin to feel angry?
What does Allah love about anger?

items.text: They know that whosoever wishes for a livelihood, or for wealth, or learning, must not merely say, "God is merciful," but must exert himself. Although the Koran says, "Every living creature's support comes from God," it is also written, "Man obtains nothing except by striving."
items.ref: al-Ghazali, The Alchemy of Happiness, ch. 2, p. 41 (tr. Claud Field, 1910)
items.topic: effort, striving, studying hard, trusting Allah and working
ask: Can I just pray to learn without studying?
Why do I need to work hard?

items.text: This world is a stage or market-place passed by pilgrims on their way to the next. It is here that they are to provide themselves with provisions for the way;
items.ref: al-Ghazali, The Alchemy of Happiness, ch. 3, p. 43 (tr. Claud Field, 1910)
items.topic: this world as a journey, preparing for the hereafter
ask: What is this life for?

items.text: The soul should take care of the body, just as a pilgrim on his way to Mecca takes care of his camel; but if the pilgrim spends his whole time in feeding and adorning his camel, the caravan will leave him behind, and he will perish in the desert.
items.ref: al-Ghazali, The Alchemy of Happiness, ch. 3, p. 44 (tr. Claud Field, 1910)
items.topic: balance, caring for the body but not too much, priorities
ask: Should I care about how I look?
items.audience: adults/older students: ends 'he will perish in the desert'

items.text: The world is like a table spread for successive relays of guests who come and go. There are gold and silver dishes, abundance of food and perfumes. The wise guest eats as much as is sufficient for him, smells the perfumes, thanks his host, and departs.
items.ref: al-Ghazali, The Alchemy of Happiness, ch. 3, p. 48 (tr. Claud Field, 1910)
items.topic: contentment, gratitude, not being greedy
ask: How much of the world should I want?

items.text: Although we have said so much against the world, it must be remembered that there are some things in the world which are not of it, such as knowledge and good deeds. A man carries what knowledge he possesses with him into the next world, and, though his good deeds have passed, yet the effect of them remains in his character.
items.ref: al-Ghazali, The Alchemy of Happiness, ch. 3, p. 49 (tr. Claud Field, 1910)
items.topic: knowledge and good deeds last, seeking knowledge
ask: What can I take with me after this life?
Why is knowledge precious?

items.text: He recognises that knowledge of God and worship are medicinal, and that ignorance and sin are deadly poisons for the soul.
items.ref: al-Ghazali, The Alchemy of Happiness, ch. 4, p. 51 (tr. Claud Field, 1910)
items.topic: knowledge and worship heal the soul
ask: Why is worship good for me?

items.text: Therefore a man should say to his soul every morning, "God has given thee twenty-four treasures; take heed lest thou lose any one of them, for thou wilt not be able to endure the regret that will follow such loss."
items.ref: al-Ghazali, The Alchemy of Happiness, ch. 6, p. 77 (tr. Claud Field, 1910)
items.topic: valuing time, every hour is a treasure
ask: Why shouldn't I waste time?

items.text: This consists in a man's remembering that God observes all his acts and thoughts. People only see the outward, while God sees both the outer and the inner man. He who really believes this will have both his outer and inner being well disciplined.
items.ref: al-Ghazali, The Alchemy of Happiness, ch. 6, p. 77 (tr. Claud Field, 1910)
items.topic: remembrance of Allah, Allah sees everything, inner and outer
ask: Does Allah see what I do when no one is watching?

items.text: Such, then, is the aim of self-examination, and the Prophet has said, "Happy is he who does now that which will benefit him after death."
items.ref: al-Ghazali, The Alchemy of Happiness, ch. 6, p. 77 (tr. Claud Field, 1910)
items.topic: self-examination, doing good now
ask: Why should I check my own actions?
items.note: Wikisource reads 'had said'; the printed page 77 of the 1910 edition (archive.org scan) reads 'has said'. Text follows the print.

items.text: Every evening he should examine his heart as to what he has done to see whether he has gained or lost in his spiritual capital.
items.ref: al-Ghazali, The Alchemy of Happiness, ch. 6, p. 83 (tr. Claud Field, 1910)
items.topic: self-examination every evening, reflecting on your day
ask: What should I think about before I sleep?

items.text: People count on their rosaries with self-satisfaction the numbers of times they have recited the name of God, but they keep no rosary for reckoning the numberless idle words they speak. Therefore the Caliph Omar said, "Weigh well your words and deeds before they be weighed at the Judgment."
items.ref: al-Ghazali, The Alchemy of Happiness, ch. 6, p. 84 (tr. Claud Field, 1910)
items.topic: guarding the tongue, idle words, Umar's advice
ask: Why should I be careful with my words?

items.text: If a man finds himself sluggish and averse from austerity and self-discipline he should consort with one who is a proficient in such practices so as to catch the contagion of his enthusiasm. One saint used to say, "When I grow lukewarm in self-discipline, I look at Muhammad Ibn Wasi, and the sight of him rekindles my fervour for at least a week."
items.ref: al-Ghazali, The Alchemy of Happiness, ch. 6, p. 85 (tr. Claud Field, 1910)
items.topic: good company, learning from righteous people, motivation
ask: What do I do when I feel lazy about worship?
Why should I sit with good people?

items.text: On one occasion Omar asked the Prophet what were the things specially to be sought in the world. He answered, "A tongue occupied in the remembrance of God, a grateful heart, and a believing wife."
items.ref: al-Ghazali, The Alchemy of Happiness, ch. 7, p. 89 (tr. Claud Field, 1910)
items.topic: gratitude, remembrance of Allah, a grateful heart (adult)
ask: What things are best to seek in this world?
items.audience: adults/older students: mentions seeking a wife

items.text: The following prayer was taught by the Prophet to his companions, "O God, grant me to love Thee and to love those who love Thee, and whatsoever brings me nearer to Thy love, and make Thy love more precious to me than cold water to the thirsty."
items.ref: al-Ghazali, The Alchemy of Happiness, ch. 8, p. 101 (tr. Claud Field, 1910)
items.topic: dua, love of Allah
ask: Is there a dua for loving Allah?

items.text: Such love is directed not towards any outward form, but towards the inner character. Even when we wish to excite love in a child towards any one, we do not describe their outward beauty of form, etc., but their inner excellencies.
items.ref: al-Ghazali, The Alchemy of Happiness, ch. 8, p. 102 (tr. Claud Field, 1910)
items.topic: good character, inner beauty matters more than looks
ask: What makes a person truly beautiful?

items.text: It is for this reason that we love Muhammad, because he is the Prophet and the Beloved of God, and the love of learned and pious men is really the love of God.
items.ref: al-Ghazali, The Alchemy of Happiness, ch. 8, p. 102 (tr. Claud Field, 1910)
items.topic: loving the Prophet, respect for scholars and teachers
ask: Why do we love and respect our teachers and scholars?

items.text: It would indeed be a wonder, if one should take refuge from the heat of the sun under the shadow of a tree and not be grateful to the tree, without which there would be no shadow at all.
items.ref: al-Ghazali, The Alchemy of Happiness, ch. 8, p. 103 (tr. Claud Field, 1910)
items.topic: gratitude to Allah, thankfulness
ask: Why should I thank Allah?

items.text: The second cause of this love is that man loves his benefactor, and in truth his only Benefactor is God, for whatever kindness he receives from any fellow-creature is due to the immediate instigation of God.
items.ref: al-Ghazali, The Alchemy of Happiness, ch. 8, p. 103 (tr. Claud Field, 1910)
items.topic: gratitude, all kindness comes from Allah
ask: Who should I thank when someone is kind to me?

items.text: The thirst for knowledge was innate in me from an early age; it was like a second nature implanted by God, without any will on my part.
items.ref: al-Ghazali, The Confessions of Al Ghazzali, “Ghazzali’s Search for Truth”, p. 13 (tr. Claud Field, 1909)
items.topic: love of knowledge, curiosity, seeking knowledge
ask: Did al-Ghazali love learning as a child?

items.text: My object in this account is to make others understand with what earnestness we should search for truth, since it leads to results we never dreamt of.
items.ref: al-Ghazali, The Confessions of Al Ghazzali, “The Subterfuges of the Sophists”, p. 19 (tr. Claud Field, 1909)
items.topic: searching for truth with effort
ask: Why should I search for the truth carefully?

items.text: It was plain to me that, in order to discover where the professors of any branch of knowledge have erred, one must make a profound study of that science; must equal, nay surpass, those who know most of it, so as to penetrate into secrets of it unknown to them.
items.ref: al-Ghazali, The Confessions of Al Ghazzali, “The Aim of Scholastic Theology and its Results”, p. 23 (tr. Claud Field, 1909)
items.topic: studying deeply before judging, mastery (adult)
ask: Should I criticise something I haven't studied?
items.audience: adults/older students: about studying philosophy; better for adults

items.text: But a liberal spirit will take as its guide this maxim of the Prince of believers, Ali the son of Abu Talib: “Do not seek for the truth by means of men; find first the truth and then you will recognise those who follow it.”
items.ref: al-Ghazali, The Confessions of Al Ghazzali, “Divisions of the Philosophic Sciences”, p. 36 (tr. Claud Field, 1909)
items.topic: judging ideas by truth, Ali's saying (adult)
ask: How do I know who to follow?
items.audience: adults/older students: abstract; better for adults

items.text: I probed the motives of my teaching and found that, in place of being sincerely consecrated to God, it was only actuated by a vain desire of honour and reputation.

Why do I study?
items.audience: adults/older students: al-Ghazali's own confession; better for older students and adults

items.text: True knowledge, on the contrary, inspires in him who is initiate in it more fear and more reverence, and raises a barrier of defence between him and sin.
items.ref: al-Ghazali, The Confessions of Al Ghazzali, “The Reality of Inspiration: its Importance for the Human Race”, p. 59 (tr. Claud Field, 1909)
items.topic: true knowledge brings humility and reverence

items.topic: his character was the Qur’an
items.ar: سألت عائشة أم المؤمنين فقلت: أخبريني عن خلق رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، فقالت: أما تقرأ القرآن؟ قلت: بلى، فقالت: كان خلقه القرآن
items.draft_en: [Saʿd ibn Hisham said:] I asked ʿAʾisha, the Mother of the Believers: “Tell me about the character of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.” She said: “Do you not read the Qur’an?” I said: “Yes, I do.” She said: “His character was the Qur’an.”
items.note: Ibn Kathir gives the chain to Saʿd ibn Hisham; the hadith is in Sahih Muslim (746).
items.text: [Saʿd ibn Hisham said:] I asked ʿAʾisha, the Mother of the Believers: “Tell me about the character of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.” She said: “Do you not read the Qur’an?” I said: “Yes, I do.” She said: “His character was the Qur’an.”

items.topic: what “his character was the Qur’an” means
items.ar: ومعنى أنه عليه السلام مهما أمره به القرآن امتثله، ومهما نهاه عنه تركه.
items.draft_en: This means that whatever the Qur’an commanded him, he carried out, and whatever it forbade him, he left.
items.note: Ibn Kathir’s own explanation. The edition prints “ومعنى أنه”.
items.text: This means that whatever the Qur’an commanded him, he carried out, and whatever it forbade him, he left.

items.topic: his character was the Qur’an: the first ten ayat of al-Muʾminun
items.ar: قلنا لعائشة يا أم المؤمنين كيف كان خلق رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم؟ قالت: كان خلق رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم القرآن ثم قالت: أتقرأ سورة المؤمنين؟ اقرأ: قد أفلح المؤمنون، إلى العشر. قالت: هكذا كان خلق رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
items.draft_en: [Zayd ibn Babanus said:] We said to ʿAʾisha: “Mother of the Believers, what was the character of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ like?” She said: “The character of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was the Qur’an.” Then she said: “Do you read Surat al-Muʾminun? Read: ‘Successful indeed are the believers’, up to the tenth ayah.” She said: “That is how the character of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was.”
items.note: From al-Bayhaqi with his chain; Ibn Kathir adds that al-Nasaʾi narrated it. The edition names the narrator “زيد بن بابنوس” (other sources: Yazid). The words of 23:1 are Pickthall’s.
items.text: [Zayd ibn Babanus said:] We said to ʿAʾisha: “Mother of the Believers, what was the character of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ like?” She said: “The character of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was the Qur’an.” Then she said: “Do you read Surat al-Muʾminun? Read: ‘Successful indeed are the believers’, up to the tenth ayah.” She said: “That is how the character of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was.”

items.topic: he chose the easier way
items.ar: ما خير رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بين أمرين إلا أخذ أيسرهما ما لم يكن إثما فإن كان إثما كان أبعد الناس منه، وما انتقم لنفسه إلا أن تنتهك حرمة الله فينتقم لله بها
items.draft_en: [ʿAʾisha said:] Whenever the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was given a choice between two things, he took the easier of them, as long as it was not a sin; if it was a sin, he was the furthest of all people from it. And he never took revenge for himself, unless something Allah made sacred was violated; then he would take revenge for Allah’s sake.
items.note: Ibn Kathir: narrated by al-Bukhari and Muslim (from Malik).
items.text: [ʿAʾisha said:] Whenever the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was given a choice between two things, he took the easier of them, as long as it was not a sin; if it was a sin, he was the furthest of all people from it. And he never took revenge for himself, unless something Allah made sacred was violated; then he would take revenge for Allah’s sake.

items.topic: he never insulted, cursed or spoke rudely
items.ar: لم يكن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم سبابا ولا لعانا ولا فاحشا
items.draft_en: [Anas ibn Malik said:] The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was not one who insulted people, nor one who cursed, nor one who spoke rudely.
items.note: Ibn Kathir: narrated by Ahmad and al-Bukhari. The rest of the sentence (“كان يقول لأحدنا عند المعاتبة: ماله تربت جبينه”, his mild words of reproach) is left out.
items.text: [Anas ibn Malik said:] The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was not one who insulted people, nor one who cursed, nor one who spoke rudely.

items.topic: he laughed with young Anas, who had not yet run his errand
items.ar: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من أحسن الناس خلقا فأرسلني يوما لحاجة فقلت: والله لا أذهب - وفي نفسي أن أذهب لما أمرني به رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم - فخرجت حتى أمر على صبيان وهم يلعبون في السوق فإذا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قد قبض بقفاي من ورائي قال: فنظرت إليه وهو يضحك فقال: يا أنيس ذهبت حيث أمرتك؟ فقلت: نعم أنا أذهب يا رسول الله.
items.draft_en: [Anas said:] The Messenger of Allah ﷺ had the best character of all people. One day he sent me on an errand, and I said: “By Allah, I will not go,” though in my heart I meant to go where the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had told me. I went out until I passed some boys playing in the market, and suddenly the Messenger of Allah ﷺ took hold of the back of my neck from behind. I looked at him, and he was laughing. He said: “Unays, did you go where I told you?” I said: “Yes, I am going, O Messenger of Allah.”
items.note: Ibn Kathir: from Sahih Muslim (ʿIkrima ibn ʿAmmar from Ishaq). “Unays” is the loving diminutive of Anas.

items.topic: nine years with Anas and never a harsh word
items.ar: قال أنس: والله لقد خدمته تسع سنين ما علمته قال لشئ صنعته لم صنعت كذا وكذا أو لشئ تركته هلا فعلت كذا وكذا
items.draft_en: Anas said: By Allah, I served him for nine years, and I never knew him to say about something I had done, “Why did you do this and that?”, or about something I had left, “Why did you not do this and that?”
items.note: Continues bx-errand (Sahih Muslim). Other reports in the same place say ten years.
items.text: Anas said: By Allah, I served him for nine years, and I never knew him to say about something I had done, “Why did you do this and that?”, or about something I had left, “Why did you not do this and that?”

items.topic: he played with little Abu ʿUmayr and asked about his bird
items.ar: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أحسن الناس خلقا وكان لي أخ يقال له أبو عمير ، قال: أحسبه قال: فطيما، قال: فكان إذا جاء رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فرآه قال: أبا عمير ما فعل النغير، قال نغر كان يلعب به
items.draft_en: [Anas said:] The Messenger of Allah ﷺ had the best character of all people. I had a little brother called Abu ʿUmayr (the narrator said: I think he said, just weaned). Whenever the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came and saw him, he would say: “Abu ʿUmayr, what did the little bird do?” It was a little bird he used to play with.
items.note: From Ahmad; Ibn Kathir: narrated by all the six books except Abu Dawud. Same event as Bukhari 6129 already in src/data/sheikh-hadith.json.

items.topic: he greeted children with salam
items.ar: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم مر على صبيان يلعبون فسلم عليهم
items.draft_en: [Anas narrated] that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ passed by some children who were playing, and he greeted them with salam.
items.note: Ibn Kathir: narrated by al-Bukhari, and by Muslim another way. Same hadith as Muslim 2168 already in src/data/sheikh-hadith.json.
items.text: [Anas narrated] that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ passed by some children who were playing, and he greeted them with salam.

items.topic: he hugged Usama and al-Hasan and prayed for them
items.ar: كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يأخذني فيقعدني على فخذه ويقعد الحسن على فخذه الأخرى ثم يضمنا ثم يقول: اللهم ارحمهما فإني أرحمهما
items.draft_en: [Usama ibn Zayd said:] The Prophet ﷺ used to take me and sit me on his thigh, and sit al-Hasan on his other thigh. Then he would hold us both close and say: “O Allah, have mercy on them, for I have mercy on them.”
items.note: Ibn Kathir: narrated by al-Bukhari. In vol. 8 (biography of Usama ibn Zayd).

items.topic: he repeated his words three times so they were understood
items.ar: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان إذا تكلم يعيد الكلمة ثلاثا لتعقل عنه
items.draft_en: [Anas narrated] that when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ spoke, he would repeat a word three times so that it would be understood from him.
items.note: Ibn Kathir quotes al-Tirmidhi: “hasan sahih gharib”. Close to Bukhari 95 (6244 in src/data/sheikh-hadith.json is related).
items.text: [Anas narrated] that when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ spoke, he would repeat a word three times so that it would be understood from him.

items.topic: he went over the Qur’an with Jibril in Ramadan
items.ar: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أجود الناس، وكان أجود ما يكون في رمضان حين يلقاه جبريل فيدارسه القرآن، فلرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أجود بالخير من الريح المرسلة
items.draft_en: [Ibn ʿAbbas said:] The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was the most generous of people, and he was at his most generous in Ramadan, when Jibril met him and went over the Qur’an with him. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was more generous with good than the wind that is sent out.
items.note: Ibn Kathir: established in the two Sahihs.
items.text: [Ibn ʿAbbas said:] The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was the most generous of people, and he was at his most generous in Ramadan, when Jibril met him and went over the Qur’an with him. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was more generous with good than the wind that is sent out.

items.topic: he loved to hear the Qur’an recited by others, and wept
items.ar: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: اقرأ علي، فقلت: اقرأ عليك وعليك أنزل؟ فقال: إني أحب أن أسمعه من غيري، قال: فقرأت سورة النساء حتى بلغت: * (فكيف إذا جئنا من كل أمة بشهيد وجئنا بك على هؤلاء شهيدا) * [الآية: 41] قال: حسبك، فالتفت فإذا عيناه تذرفان
items.draft_en: [ʿAbdullah ibn Masʿud said:] The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Recite to me.” I said: “Shall I recite to you, when it was sent down to you?” He said: “I love to hear it from someone else.” So I recited Surat al-Nisaʾ until I reached: “But how (will it be with them) when We bring of every people a witness, and We bring thee (O Muhammad) a witness against these?” [ayah 41]. He said: “That is enough.” I turned, and his eyes were flowing with tears.
items.note: Ibn Kathir: narrated by al-Bukhari. The ayah (4:41) is given in Pickthall’s words. The Arabic contains Qur’an text in the edition’s spelling (unvowelled), not the Tanzil text.
items.text: [ʿAbdullah ibn Masʿud said:] The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Recite to me.” I said: “Shall I recite to you, when it was sent down to you?” He said: “I love to hear it from someone else.” So I recited Surat al-Nisaʾ until I reached: “But how (will it be with them) when We bring of every people a witness, and We bring thee (O Muhammad) a witness against these?” [ayah 41]. He said: “That is enough.” I turned, and his eyes were flowing with tears.

items.topic: he recited a surah so slowly it became longer than a longer one
items.ar: قالت: وكان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقرأ السورة فيرتلها حتى تكون أطول من أطول منها
items.draft_en: She said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ would recite a surah, reciting it slowly and clearly (tartil), until it became longer than a surah longer than it.
items.note: Doubtful attribution: in this place “she” is ʿAʾisha (the paragraph begins “قالت عائشة”), but in Sahih Muslim (733) these words are from Hafsa. Ibn Kathir summarises without chains here. Please check before use.
items.text: She said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ would recite a surah, reciting it slowly and clearly (tartil), until it became longer than a surah longer than it.

items.topic: the most beautiful voice; he recited with tartil as Allah commanded
items.ar: قال جبير بن مطعم: قرأ رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في المغرب بالتين والزيتون، فما سمعت صوتا أطيب من صوته صلى الله عليه وسلم، وكان يقرأ ترتيلا كما أمره الله عز وجل بذلك
items.draft_en: Jubayr ibn Mutʿim said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited al-Tin wa’l-Zaytun in the sunset prayer, and I never heard a voice more pleasing than his ﷺ. And he used to recite with tartil, as Allah, Mighty and Majestic, commanded him.
items.note: Doubtful, proposed as “reported”: in al-Bukhari and Muslim the words about al-Tin and the beautiful voice are from al-Baraʾ ibn ʿAzib; Jubayr ibn Mutʿim reported hearing al-Tur. The passage is in a comparison of the Prophet ﷺ with Dawud (quoting Ibn Hamid), and its last clause is commentary.
items.text: Jubayr ibn Mutʿim said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited al-Tin wa’l-Zaytun in the sunset prayer, and I never heard a voice more pleasing than his ﷺ. And he used to recite with tartil, as Allah, Mighty and Majestic, commanded him.

items.ar: أَوْ زِدْ عَلَيْهِ وَرَتِّلِ ٱلْقُرْءَانَ تَرْتِيلًا
items.text: Or add (a little) thereto - and chant the Qur'an in measure,
items.topic: reciting the Qur’an slowly and clearly (tartil)
ask: how should I recite the Quran
should I recite fast or slowly
what is tartil
items.note: Begins mid-sentence: “Or add (a little) thereto” continues 73:2–3 (keeping vigil at night).

items.ar: وَلَقَدْ يَسَّرْنَا ٱلْقُرْءَانَ لِلذِّكْرِ فَهَلْ مِن مُّدَّكِرٍ
items.text: And in truth We have made the Qur'an easy to remember; but is there any that remembereth?
items.topic: the Qur’an is made easy to remember
ask: is the Quran easy to remember
can I memorise the Quran
is memorising the Quran too hard for me

items.ar: فَتَعَـٰلَى ٱللَّهُ ٱلْمَلِكُ ٱلْحَقُّ ۗ وَلَا تَعْجَلْ بِٱلْقُرْءَانِ مِن قَبْلِ أَن يُقْضَىٰٓ إِلَيْكَ وَحْيُهُۥ ۖ وَقُل رَّبِّ زِدْنِى عِلْمًا
items.text: Then exalted be Allah, the True King! And hasten not (O Muhammad) with the Qur'an ere its revelation hath been perfected unto thee, and say: My Lord! Increase me in knowledge.
items.topic: a dua for more knowledge
ask: what dua can I say to learn more
is there a dua for knowledge
what should I say before I study
items.note: Long; the dua is its last words.

items.ar: لَا تُحَرِّكْ بِهِۦ لِسَانَكَ لِتَعْجَلَ بِهِۦٓ
items.text: Stir not thy tongue herewith to hasten it.
items.topic: not hurrying the tongue when reciting
ask: should I rush when I recite
why should I not hurry my recitation

items.ar: وَقُرْءَانًا فَرَقْنَـٰهُ لِتَقْرَأَهُۥ عَلَى ٱلنَّاسِ عَلَىٰ مُكْثٍ وَنَزَّلْنَـٰهُ تَنزِيلًا
items.text: And (it is) a Qur'an that We have divided, that thou mayst recite it unto mankind at intervals, and We have revealed it by (successive) revelation.
items.topic: the Qur’an was revealed in parts, to be recited bit by bit
ask: why was the Quran revealed in parts
was the Quran revealed all at once

items.ar: وَإِذَا قُرِئَ ٱلْقُرْءَانُ فَٱسْتَمِعُوا۟ لَهُۥ وَأَنصِتُوا۟ لَعَلَّكُمْ تُرْحَمُونَ
items.text: And when the Qur'an is recited, give ear to it and pay heed, that ye may obtain mercy.
items.topic: listening quietly when the Qur’an is recited
ask: what should I do when someone recites the Quran
should I be quiet when the Quran is recited

items.ar: فَإِذَا قَرَأْتَ ٱلْقُرْءَانَ فَٱسْتَعِذْ بِٱللَّهِ مِنَ ٱلشَّيْطَـٰنِ ٱلرَّجِيمِ
items.text: And when thou recitest the Qur'an, seek refuge in Allah from Satan the outcast.
items.topic: seeking refuge in Allah before reciting
ask: what do I say before I recite the Quran
why do we say audhu billah before reading

items.ar: ٱقْرَأْ بِٱسْمِ رَبِّكَ ٱلَّذِى خَلَقَ
items.text: Read: In the name of thy Lord Who createth,
items.topic: the first word revealed: read
ask: what does iqra mean
what does the first ayah of Surah al-Alaq say

items.ar: ٱلَّذِى عَلَّمَ بِٱلْقَلَمِ عَلَّمَ ٱلْإِنسَـٰنَ مَا لَمْ يَعْلَمْ
items.text: Who teacheth by the pen, Teacheth man that which he knew not.
items.topic: Allah taught by the pen what we did not know
ask: who teaches us
why is writing and learning important

items.ar: ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنُ عَلَّمَ ٱلْقُرْءَانَ
items.text: The Beneficent Hath made known the Qur'an.
items.topic: the Most Merciful taught the Qur’an
ask: who taught the Quran
where does the Quran come from

items.ar: كِتَـٰبٌ أَنزَلْنَـٰهُ إِلَيْكَ مُبَـٰرَكٌ لِّيَدَّبَّرُوٓا۟ ءَايَـٰتِهِۦ وَلِيَتَذَكَّرَ أُو۟لُوا۟ ٱلْأَلْبَـٰبِ
items.text: (This is) a Scripture that We have revealed unto thee, full of blessing, that they may ponder its revelations, and that men of understanding may reflect.
items.topic: the Qur’an is blessed, so think about its meaning
ask: why should I think about the meaning of the Quran
is the Quran a blessed book

items.ar: أَفَلَا يَتَدَبَّرُونَ ٱلْقُرْءَانَ أَمْ عَلَىٰ قُلُوبٍ أَقْفَالُهَآ
items.text: Will they then not meditate on the Qur'an, or are there locks on the hearts?
items.topic: pondering the Qur’an
ask: should I think about what the Quran means
why should we reflect on the Quran

items.ar: وَنُنَزِّلُ مِنَ ٱلْقُرْءَانِ مَا هُوَ شِفَآءٌ وَرَحْمَةٌ لِّلْمُؤْمِنِينَ ۙ وَلَا يَزِيدُ ٱلظَّـٰلِمِينَ إِلَّا خَسَارًا
items.text: And We reveal of the Qur'an that which is a healing and a mercy for believers though it increase the evil-doers in naught save ruin.
items.topic: the Qur’an is a healing and a mercy
ask: is the Quran a healing
how does the Quran help believers

items.ar: يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّاسُ قَدْ جَآءَتْكُم مَّوْعِظَةٌ مِّن رَّبِّكُمْ وَشِفَآءٌ لِّمَا فِى ٱلصُّدُورِ وَهُدًى وَرَحْمَةٌ لِّلْمُؤْمِنِينَ
items.text: O mankind! There hath come unto you an exhortation from your Lord, a balm for that which is in the breasts, a guidance and a mercy for believers.
items.topic: the Qur’an heals what is in the hearts
ask: can the Quran help when my heart is sad
what is the Quran for

items.ar: أَمَّنْ هُوَ قَـٰنِتٌ ءَانَآءَ ٱلَّيْلِ سَاجِدًا وَقَآئِمًا يَحْذَرُ ٱلْـَٔاخِرَةَ وَيَرْجُوا۟ رَحْمَةَ رَبِّهِۦ ۗ قُلْ هَلْ يَسْتَوِى ٱلَّذِينَ يَعْلَمُونَ وَٱلَّذِينَ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ ۗ إِنَّمَا يَتَذَكَّرُ أُو۟لُوا۟ ٱلْأَلْبَـٰبِ
items.text: Is he who payeth adoration in the watches of the night, prostrate and standing, bewaring of the Hereafter and hoping for the mercy of his Lord, (to be accounted equal with a disbeliever)? Say (unto them, O Muhammad): Are those who know equal with those who know not? But only men of understanding will pay heed.
items.topic: those who know and those who do not are not equal
ask: why is knowledge important
are people who learn better
why should I learn

items.ar: يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓا۟ إِذَا قِيلَ لَكُمْ تَفَسَّحُوا۟ فِى ٱلْمَجَـٰلِسِ فَٱفْسَحُوا۟ يَفْسَحِ ٱللَّهُ لَكُمْ ۖ وَإِذَا قِيلَ ٱنشُزُوا۟ فَٱنشُزُوا۟ يَرْفَعِ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ مِنكُمْ وَٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُوا۟ ٱلْعِلْمَ دَرَجَـٰتٍ ۚ وَٱللَّهُ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ خَبِيرٌ
items.text: O ye who believe! when it is said unto you: Make room! in assemblies, then make room; Allah will make way for you (hereafter). And when it is said: Come up higher! go up higher; Allah will exalt those who believe among you, and those who have knowledge, to high ranks. Allah is informed of what ye do.
items.topic: making room in gatherings; Allah raises those with knowledge
ask: does Allah raise people with knowledge
should I make room for others when they sit down
items.note: Tanzil en.pickthall 58:11 differs: “O ye who believe! when it is said unto you, Make room! in assemblies, then make room; Allah will make way for you (hereafter). And when it is said, Come up higher! go up higher; Allah will exalt those who believe among you, and those who have knowledge, to high ranks. Allah is Informed of what ye do.”.

items.ar: يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ ٱسْتَعِينُوا۟ بِٱلصَّبْرِ وَٱلصَّلَوٰةِ ۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ مَعَ ٱلصَّـٰبِرِينَ
items.text: O ye who believe! Seek help in steadfastness and prayer. Lo! Allah is with the steadfast.
items.topic: seek help through patience and prayer
ask: what should I do when things are hard
how can I be patient
is Allah with the patient

items.ar: قُلْ يَـٰعِبَادِ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ ٱتَّقُوا۟ رَبَّكُمْ ۚ لِلَّذِينَ أَحْسَنُوا۟ فِى هَـٰذِهِ ٱلدُّنْيَا حَسَنَةٌ ۗ وَأَرْضُ ٱللَّهِ وَٰسِعَةٌ ۗ إِنَّمَا يُوَفَّى ٱلصَّـٰبِرُونَ أَجْرَهُم بِغَيْرِ حِسَابٍ
items.text: Say: O My bondmen who believe! Observe your duty to your Lord. For those who do good in this world there is good, and Allah's earth is spacious. Verily the steadfast will be paid their wages without stint.
items.topic: the patient are rewarded without measure
ask: what is the reward for patience
is being patient worth it

items.ar: فَإِنَّ مَعَ ٱلْعُسْرِ يُسْرًا
items.text: But lo! with hardship goeth ease,
items.topic: with hardship comes ease
ask: will things get easier
what if things are hard for me

items.ar: وَٱصْبِرْ وَمَا صَبْرُكَ إِلَّا بِٱللَّهِ ۚ وَلَا تَحْزَنْ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا تَكُ فِى ضَيْقٍ مِّمَّا يَمْكُرُونَ
items.text: Endure thou patiently (O Muhammad). Thine endurance is only by (the help of) Allah. Grieve not for them, and be not in distress because of that which they devise.
items.topic: patience comes with Allah’s help
ask: how can I be patient
where does patience come from

items.ar: وَإِذْ تَأَذَّنَ رَبُّكُمْ لَئِن شَكَرْتُمْ لَأَزِيدَنَّكُمْ ۖ وَلَئِن كَفَرْتُمْ إِنَّ عَذَابِى لَشَدِيدٌ
items.text: And when your Lord proclaimed: If ye give thanks, I will give you more; but if ye are thankless, lo! My punishment is dire.
items.topic: if you are thankful, Allah gives you more
ask: why should I be thankful
what happens when I say alhamdulillah
why should I thank Allah
items.note: Ends “My punishment is dire”.

items.ar: فَٱذْكُرُونِىٓ أَذْكُرْكُمْ وَٱشْكُرُوا۟ لِى وَلَا تَكْفُرُونِ
items.text: Therefore remember Me, I will remember you. Give thanks to Me, and reject not Me.
items.topic: remember Allah and He remembers you; be thankful
ask: does Allah remember me
what happens when I remember Allah

items.ar: وَلَقَدْ ءَاتَيْنَا لُقْمَـٰنَ ٱلْحِكْمَةَ أَنِ ٱشْكُرْ لِلَّهِ ۚ وَمَن يَشْكُرْ فَإِنَّمَا يَشْكُرُ لِنَفْسِهِۦ ۖ وَمَن كَفَرَ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَنِىٌّ حَمِيدٌ
items.text: And verily We gave Luqman wisdom, saying: Give thanks unto Allah; and whosoever giveth thanks, he giveth thanks for (the good of) his soul. And whosoever refuseth - Lo! Allah is Absolute, Owner of Praise.
items.topic: Luqman’s wisdom: be thankful to Allah
ask: who was Luqman
who benefits when I am thankful

items.ar: وَقَضَىٰ رَبُّكَ أَلَّا تَعْبُدُوٓا۟ إِلَّآ إِيَّاهُ وَبِٱلْوَٰلِدَيْنِ إِحْسَـٰنًا ۚ إِمَّا يَبْلُغَنَّ عِندَكَ ٱلْكِبَرَ أَحَدُهُمَآ أَوْ كِلَاهُمَا فَلَا تَقُل لَّهُمَآ أُفٍّ وَلَا تَنْهَرْهُمَا وَقُل لَّهُمَا قَوْلًا كَرِيمًا
items.text: Thy Lord hath decreed, that ye worship none save Him, and (that ye show) kindness to parents. If one of them or both of them attain old age with thee, say not "Fie" unto them nor repulse them, but speak unto them a gracious word.
items.topic: kindness to parents; never say “uff” to them
ask: how should I treat my parents
can I be rude to my parents
how should I speak to my parents

items.ar: وَٱخْفِضْ لَهُمَا جَنَاحَ ٱلذُّلِّ مِنَ ٱلرَّحْمَةِ وَقُل رَّبِّ ٱرْحَمْهُمَا كَمَا رَبَّيَانِى صَغِيرًا
items.text: And lower unto them the wing of submission through mercy, and say: My Lord! Have mercy on them both as they did care for me when I was little.
items.topic: humility to parents and a dua for them
ask: what dua can I make for my parents
how can I make dua for my mum and dad

items.ar: قُلْ يَـٰعِبَادِىَ ٱلَّذِينَ أَسْرَفُوا۟ عَلَىٰٓ أَنفُسِهِمْ لَا تَقْنَطُوا۟ مِن رَّحْمَةِ ٱللَّهِ ۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَغْفِرُ ٱلذُّنُوبَ جَمِيعًا ۚ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلْغَفُورُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ
items.text: Say: O My slaves who have been prodigal to their own hurt! Despair not of the mercy of Allah, Who forgiveth all sins. Lo! He is the Forgiving, the Merciful.
items.topic: never lose hope in Allah’s mercy
ask: will Allah forgive me
what if I did something wrong
can Allah forgive all sins

items.ar: وَمَآ أَرْسَلْنَـٰكَ إِلَّا رَحْمَةً لِّلْعَـٰلَمِينَ
items.text: We sent thee not save as a mercy for the peoples.
items.topic: the Prophet ﷺ was sent as a mercy
ask: why was the Prophet sent
was the Prophet a mercy

items.ar: فَبِمَا رَحْمَةٍ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ لِنتَ لَهُمْ ۖ وَلَوْ كُنتَ فَظًّا غَلِيظَ ٱلْقَلْبِ لَٱنفَضُّوا۟ مِنْ حَوْلِكَ ۖ فَٱعْفُ عَنْهُمْ وَٱسْتَغْفِرْ لَهُمْ وَشَاوِرْهُمْ فِى ٱلْأَمْرِ ۖ فَإِذَا عَزَمْتَ فَتَوَكَّلْ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ ۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُحِبُّ ٱلْمُتَوَكِّلِينَ
items.text: It was by the mercy of Allah that thou wast lenient with them (O Muhammad), for if thou hadst been stern and fierce of heart they would have dispersed from round about thee. So pardon them and ask forgiveness for them and consult with them upon the conduct of affairs. And when thou art resolved, then put thy trust in Allah. Lo! Allah loveth those who put their trust (in Him).
items.topic: the Prophet’s ﷺ gentleness drew people to him
ask: why was the Prophet gentle
why should I be gentle
was the Prophet kind to people

items.ar: وَإِذَا جَآءَكَ ٱلَّذِينَ يُؤْمِنُونَ بِـَٔايَـٰتِنَا فَقُلْ سَلَـٰمٌ عَلَيْكُمْ ۖ كَتَبَ رَبُّكُمْ عَلَىٰ نَفْسِهِ ٱلرَّحْمَةَ ۖ أَنَّهُۥ مَنْ عَمِلَ مِنكُمْ سُوٓءًۢا بِجَهَـٰلَةٍ ثُمَّ تَابَ مِنۢ بَعْدِهِۦ وَأَصْلَحَ فَأَنَّهُۥ غَفُورٌ رَّحِيمٌ
items.text: And when those who believe in Our revelations come unto thee, say: Peace be unto you! Your Lord hath prescribed for Himself mercy, that whoso of you doeth evil through ignorance and repenteth afterward thereof and doeth right, (for him) lo! He is Forgiving, Merciful.
items.topic: Allah has written mercy upon Himself; repenting after a mistake
ask: what if I make a mistake and say sorry to Allah
is Allah merciful

items.ar: وَمَآ أُمِرُوٓا۟ إِلَّا لِيَعْبُدُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ مُخْلِصِينَ لَهُ ٱلدِّينَ حُنَفَآءَ وَيُقِيمُوا۟ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَيُؤْتُوا۟ ٱلزَّكَوٰةَ ۚ وَذَٰلِكَ دِينُ ٱلْقَيِّمَةِ
items.text: And they are ordered naught else than to serve Allah, keeping religion pure for Him, as men by nature upright, and to establish worship and to pay the poor-due. That is true religion.
items.topic: worshipping Allah sincerely
ask: what does it mean to be sincere
who should I worship for

items.ar: قُلْ إِنَّ صَلَاتِى وَنُسُكِى وَمَحْيَاىَ وَمَمَاتِى لِلَّهِ رَبِّ ٱلْعَـٰلَمِينَ
items.text: Say: Lo! my worship and my sacrifice and my living and my dying are for Allah, Lord of the Worlds.
items.topic: all my prayer and my life are for Allah (intention)
ask: who should I pray for
why do we do good deeds
what should my intention be

items.ar: وَإِذْ أَخَذْنَا مِيثَـٰقَ بَنِىٓ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ لَا تَعْبُدُونَ إِلَّا ٱللَّهَ وَبِٱلْوَٰلِدَيْنِ إِحْسَانًا وَذِى ٱلْقُرْبَىٰ وَٱلْيَتَـٰمَىٰ وَٱلْمَسَـٰكِينِ وَقُولُوا۟ لِلنَّاسِ حُسْنًا وَأَقِيمُوا۟ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَءَاتُوا۟ ٱلزَّكَوٰةَ ثُمَّ تَوَلَّيْتُمْ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا مِّنكُمْ وَأَنتُم مُّعْرِضُونَ
items.text: And (remember) when We made a covenant with the Children of Israel, (saying): Worship none save Allah (only), and be good to parents and to kindred and to orphans and the needy, and speak kindly to mankind; and establish worship and pay the poor-due. Then, after that, ye slid back, save a few of you, being averse.
items.topic: be good to parents, orphans and the needy, and speak kindly to people
ask: how should I speak to people
who should I be good to
items.note: Context: the covenant with the Children of Israel; ends “ye slid back, save a few of you”.

items.ar: وَقُل لِّعِبَادِى يَقُولُوا۟ ٱلَّتِى هِىَ أَحْسَنُ ۚ إِنَّ ٱلشَّيْطَـٰنَ يَنزَغُ بَيْنَهُمْ ۚ إِنَّ ٱلشَّيْطَـٰنَ كَانَ لِلْإِنسَـٰنِ عَدُوًّا مُّبِينًا
items.text: Tell My bondmen to speak that which is kindlier. Lo! the devil soweth discord among them. Lo! the devil is for man an open foe.
items.topic: say what is best; Satan stirs up quarrels
ask: how should I talk to others
why do people fight
what words should I use

items.ar: يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ ٱتَّقُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ وَقُولُوا۟ قَوْلًا سَدِيدًا
items.text: O ye who believe! Guard your duty to Allah, and speak words straight to the point;
items.topic: speak words that are right and true
ask: what kind of words should I say
should I speak the truth

items.ar: وَٱقْصِدْ فِى مَشْيِكَ وَٱغْضُضْ مِن صَوْتِكَ ۚ إِنَّ أَنكَرَ ٱلْأَصْوَٰتِ لَصَوْتُ ٱلْحَمِيرِ
items.text: Be modest in thy bearing and subdue thy voice. Lo! the harshest of all voices is the voice of the ass.
items.topic: Luqman’s advice: walk modestly and lower your voice
ask: should I shout
how should I speak to people
should I talk loudly

items.ar: أَلَمْ تَرَ كَيْفَ ضَرَبَ ٱللَّهُ مَثَلًا كَلِمَةً طَيِّبَةً كَشَجَرَةٍ طَيِّبَةٍ أَصْلُهَا ثَابِتٌ وَفَرْعُهَا فِى ٱلسَّمَآءِ
items.text: Seest thou not how Allah coineth a similitude: A goodly saying, as a goodly tree, its root set firm, its branches reaching into heaven,
items.topic: a good word is like a good tree
ask: why are good words important
what is a good word like

items.ar: وَعِبَادُ ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنِ ٱلَّذِينَ يَمْشُونَ عَلَى ٱلْأَرْضِ هَوْنًا وَإِذَا خَاطَبَهُمُ ٱلْجَـٰهِلُونَ قَالُوا۟ سَلَـٰمًا
items.text: The (faithful) slaves of the Beneficent are they who walk upon the earth modestly, and when the foolish ones address them answer: Peace;
items.topic: the servants of the Most Merciful walk humbly and answer with peace
ask: what should I do if someone is rude to me
how should I walk
who are the servants of the Most Merciful

items.ar: وَلَا تَسْتَوِى ٱلْحَسَنَةُ وَلَا ٱلسَّيِّئَةُ ۚ ٱدْفَعْ بِٱلَّتِى هِىَ أَحْسَنُ فَإِذَا ٱلَّذِى بَيْنَكَ وَبَيْنَهُۥ عَدَٰوَةٌ كَأَنَّهُۥ وَلِىٌّ حَمِيمٌ
items.text: The good deed and the evil deed are not alike. Repel the evil deed with one which is better, then lo! he, between whom and thee there was enmity (will become) as though he was a bosom friend.
items.topic: answer bad with what is better and enemies become friends
ask: what should I do if someone is mean to me
how can I make an enemy a friend

items.ar: ٱتْلُ مَآ أُوحِىَ إِلَيْكَ مِنَ ٱلْكِتَـٰبِ وَأَقِمِ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ ۖ إِنَّ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ تَنْهَىٰ عَنِ ٱلْفَحْشَآءِ وَٱلْمُنكَرِ ۗ وَلَذِكْرُ ٱللَّهِ أَكْبَرُ ۗ وَٱللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ مَا تَصْنَعُونَ
items.text: Recite that which hath been inspired in thee of the Scripture, and establish worship. Lo! worship preserveth from lewdness and iniquity, but verily remembrance of Allah is more important. And Allah knoweth what ye do.
items.topic: prayer keeps us from bad deeds
ask: why do we pray
what does salah do for us

items.ar: حَـٰفِظُوا۟ عَلَى ٱلصَّلَوَٰتِ وَٱلصَّلَوٰةِ ٱلْوُسْطَىٰ وَقُومُوا۟ لِلَّهِ قَـٰنِتِينَ
items.text: Be guardians of your prayers, and of the midmost prayer, and stand up with devotion to Allah.
items.topic: guard your prayers
ask: should I look after my prayers
is it important to pray on time

items.ar: قَدْ أَفْلَحَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنُونَ ٱلَّذِينَ هُمْ فِى صَلَاتِهِمْ خَـٰشِعُونَ
items.text: Successful indeed are the believers Who are humble in their prayers,
items.topic: successful are the believers who are humble in prayer
ask: who are the successful people
how should I pray

items.ar: وَقَالَ رَبُّكُمُ ٱدْعُونِىٓ أَسْتَجِبْ لَكُمْ ۚ إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يَسْتَكْبِرُونَ عَنْ عِبَادَتِى سَيَدْخُلُونَ جَهَنَّمَ دَاخِرِينَ
items.text: And your Lord hath said: Pray unto Me and I will hear your prayer. Lo! those who scorn My service, they will enter hell, disgraced.
items.topic: call on Allah and He answers
ask: does Allah answer dua
should I make dua
does Allah hear me when I ask
items.note: Ends with a warning about Hell; may not suit young children.

items.ar: وَمِنْهُم مَّن يَقُولُ رَبَّنَآ ءَاتِنَا فِى ٱلدُّنْيَا حَسَنَةً وَفِى ٱلْـَٔاخِرَةِ حَسَنَةً وَقِنَا عَذَابَ ٱلنَّارِ
items.text: And of them (also) is he who saith: "Our Lord! Give unto us in the world that which is good and in the Hereafter that which is good, and guard us from the doom of Fire."
items.topic: the dua for good in this world and the next
ask: what is a good dua to make
what dua can I say every day

items.ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ يَقُولُونَ رَبَّنَا هَبْ لَنَا مِنْ أَزْوَٰجِنَا وَذُرِّيَّـٰتِنَا قُرَّةَ أَعْيُنٍ وَٱجْعَلْنَا لِلْمُتَّقِينَ إِمَامًا
items.text: And who say: Our Lord! Vouchsafe us comfort of our wives and of our offspring, and make us patterns for (all) those who ward off (evil).
items.topic: a dua for one’s family
ask: what dua can I make for my family
items.note: Pickthall: “comfort of our wives and of our offspring”; check it suits a child asking about family.

items.ar: رَبِّ ٱجْعَلْنِى مُقِيمَ ٱلصَّلَوٰةِ وَمِن ذُرِّيَّتِى ۚ رَبَّنَا وَتَقَبَّلْ دُعَآءِ
items.text: My Lord! Make me to establish proper worship, and some of my posterity (also); our Lord! and accept my prayer.
items.topic: Ibrahim’s dua to keep up prayer
ask: is there a dua to help me pray
what dua did Ibrahim make

items.ar: قَالَ رَبِّ ٱشْرَحْ لِى صَدْرِى وَيَسِّرْ لِىٓ أَمْرِى وَٱحْلُلْ عُقْدَةً مِّن لِّسَانِى يَفْقَهُوا۟ قَوْلِى
items.text: (Moses) said: My Lord! relieve my mind And ease my task for me; And loose a knot from my tongue, That they may understand my saying.
items.topic: Musa’s dua: ease my task and loosen my tongue
ask: what dua can I say before I recite
is there a dua for speaking clearly
what dua can I say before a test

items.ar: وَلَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا ٱلْإِنسَـٰنَ وَنَعْلَمُ مَا تُوَسْوِسُ بِهِۦ نَفْسُهُۥ ۖ وَنَحْنُ أَقْرَبُ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ حَبْلِ ٱلْوَرِيدِ
items.text: We verily created man and We know what his soul whispereth to him, and We are nearer to him than his jugular vein.
items.topic: Allah is closer than our jugular vein
ask: is Allah close to me
does Allah know what I am thinking

items.ar: فَمَن يَعْمَلْ مِثْقَالَ ذَرَّةٍ خَيْرًا يَرَهُۥ
items.text: And whoso doeth good an atom's weight will see it then,
items.topic: even an atom’s weight of good is seen
ask: does a small good deed count
will Allah see my good deeds

items.ar: وَإِذَا حُيِّيتُم بِتَحِيَّةٍ فَحَيُّوا۟ بِأَحْسَنَ مِنْهَآ أَوْ رُدُّوهَآ ۗ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَىْءٍ حَسِيبًا
items.text: When ye are greeted with a greeting, greet ye with a better than it or return it. Lo! Allah taketh count of all things.
items.topic: return a greeting with a better one
ask: how should I answer salam
what do I say when someone says salam

items.ar: قَوْلٌ مَّعْرُوفٌ وَمَغْفِرَةٌ خَيْرٌ مِّن صَدَقَةٍ يَتْبَعُهَآ أَذًى ۗ وَٱللَّهُ غَنِىٌّ حَلِيمٌ
items.text: A kind word with forgiveness is better than almsgiving followed by injury. Allah is Absolute, Clement.
items.topic: a kind word is better than charity followed by hurt
ask: is a kind word better than charity
is a kind word a good deed

items.ar: يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ ٱذْكُرُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ ذِكْرًا كَثِيرًا
items.text: O ye who believe! Remember Allah with much remembrance.
items.topic: remember Allah often
ask: how often should I remember Allah
should I do dhikr a lot

items.ar: هُوَ ٱلَّذِى بَعَثَ فِى ٱلْأُمِّيِّـۧنَ رَسُولًا مِّنْهُمْ يَتْلُوا۟ عَلَيْهِمْ ءَايَـٰتِهِۦ وَيُزَكِّيهِمْ وَيُعَلِّمُهُمُ ٱلْكِتَـٰبَ وَٱلْحِكْمَةَ وَإِن كَانُوا۟ مِن قَبْلُ لَفِى ضَلَـٰلٍ مُّبِينٍ
items.text: He it is Who hath sent among the unlettered ones a messenger of their own, to recite unto them His revelations and to make them grow, and to teach them the Scripture and wisdom, though heretofore they were indeed in error manifest,
items.topic: the Prophet ﷺ recited, purified and taught the Book and wisdom
ask: what did the Prophet teach
was the Prophet a teacher

items.ar: وَإِنَّكَ لَعَلَىٰ خُلُقٍ عَظِيمٍ
items.text: And lo! thou art of a tremendous nature.
items.topic: the Prophet’s ﷺ great character
ask: what was the Prophet’s character like
did the Prophet have good manners

items.ar: لَّقَدْ كَانَ لَكُمْ فِى رَسُولِ ٱللَّهِ أُسْوَةٌ حَسَنَةٌ لِّمَن كَانَ يَرْجُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ وَٱلْيَوْمَ ٱلْـَٔاخِرَ وَذَكَرَ ٱللَّهَ كَثِيرًا
items.text: Verily in the messenger of Allah ye have a good example for him who looketh unto Allah and the Last Day, and remembereth Allah much.
items.topic: the Prophet ﷺ is the best example
ask: who is the best example to follow
why should I follow the Prophet
